root_cause.text: The netfilter IPv6 routing-header matcher in `ip6t_rt` failed to validate the user-controlled `rtinfo->addrnr` field in `rt_mt6_check()`, allowing `rt_mt6()` to use an out-of-bounds index/count against the fixed-size `rtinfo->addrs[]` array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (rtinfo->addrnr > IP6T_RT_HOPS) ... return -EINVAL;` to `rt_mt6_check()`, and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state that "`rt_mt6()` expects addrnr to stay within the bounds of `rtinfo->addrs[]`" and that malformed rules previously could supply an out-of-range value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check in rt_mt6_check() to reject IPv6 route matches with too many addresses.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added in rt_mt6_check() to test whether rtinfo->addrnr exceeds IP6T_RT_HOPS, and if so, log "too many addresses specified" with pr_debug() and return -EINVAL.
intent_record.how: This change rejects rule configurations that specify more IPv6 routing addresses than the supported hop limit, preventing invalid match parameters from being accepted and stopping later code from operating on out-of-range address counts.

grouping_result.intent: Add a bounds check in rt_mt6_check() to reject IPv6 route matches with too many addresses.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by validating the user-controlled rtinfo->addrnr in rt_mt6_check() and rejecting oversized address counts before rt_mt6() can index past the fixed-size rtinfo->addrs[] array.

candidates.rationale: This validation block in rt_mt6_check() continued with other field checks but, before the fix, omitted any validation of the user-controlled rtinfo->addrnr value. The vulnerability stems from this check path allowing malformed addrnr to pass, leading to later out-of-bounds use of rtinfo->addrs[].

vuln_statements.explanation: This validation condition is part of rt_mt6_check(), the gatekeeper for user-supplied match parameters. In the vulnerable pre-fix code, this check path validated other fields but did not validate the user-controlled rtinfo->addrnr field, allowing oversized addrnr values to pass and later be used by rt_mt6() as an out-of-bounds index/count for the fixed-size rtinfo->addrs[] array.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes both the packet-matching logic in `match()` and the rule-validation logic in `checkentry()`, which is sufficient to determine the issue. The root cause is missing validation of the user-controlled `rtinfo->addrnr` against the fixed-size `rtinfo->addrs[]` array in `checkentry()`. In this version, `checkentry()` only validates `matchinfosize`, `invflags`, and a type/flag combination: `if (matchinfosize != IP6T_ALIGN(sizeof(struct ip6t_rt)))`, `if (rtinfo->invflags & ~IP6T_RT_INV_MASK)`, and `if ((rtinfo->flags & (IP6T_RT_RES | IP6T_RT_FST_MASK)) && ... )`, then `return 1;`. There is no check on `rtinfo->addrnr`. Meanwhile, `match()` uses `rtinfo->addrnr` to control access to `rtinfo->addrs[]`: in non-strict mode it compares `if (ipv6_addr_equal(ap, &rtinfo->addrs[i])) { i++; }` and stops only when `i == rtinfo->addrnr`; in strict mode it loops `for (temp = 0; temp < rtinfo->addrnr; temp++)` and accesses `rtinfo->addrs[temp]`. Because `addrnr` is not bounded in `checkentry()`, these accesses can go past the fixed-size array. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it contains both the packet-matching logic that uses `rtinfo->addrnr` and the validation function `checkentry()` that should constrain user-controlled fields. The vulnerable construct is present: `match()` indexes and bounds its loops using `rtinfo->addrnr` against the packet header count only, not against the fixed-size `rtinfo->addrs[]` array. In the non-strict path, `if (rtinfo->addrnr > (unsigned int)((hdrlen-8)/16)) return 0;` is followed by `if (ipv6_addr_equal(ap, &rtinfo->addrs[i])) { i++; }` and loop termination `if (i==rtinfo->addrnr) break;`, so `i` can advance up to `rtinfo->addrnr` and access `rtinfo->addrs[i]` without any array-size validation. In the strict path, `for (temp=0; temp<rtinfo->addrnr; temp++)` uses `if (!ipv6_addr_equal(ap, &rtinfo->addrs[temp])) break;`, again indexing `rtinfo->addrs[temp]` based on unchecked `addrnr`. The supposed checker `checkentry()` validates `matchinfosize`, `invflags`, and some flag/type combinations, but it does not validate `rtinfo->addrnr` at all. Since the root cause is missing validation of user-controlled `rtinfo->addrnr` in the check function, and that validation is absent here, this function set contains the bug and does not contain the fix.
